original defects closed.defect: Scalar binary64 bins can include both ordinary UTC and genuine leap time, at leap start as well as midnight.
original defects closed.closure: Reject closed rounding bins contacting either known positive leap boundary with AmbiguousScalarJD/code ambiguous_scalar_jd. Endpoints use adjacent binary64 half-gaps as separate Time components; no scalar addition, epsilon, rounding, clamp or whole-second snap.

original defects closed.defect: Neither the time adapter nor HTTP/provider resolver could preserve two-part input.
original defects closed.closure: Frozen hashable TwoPartJD retains Astropy TDB jd1/jd2 through /solar/realtime/aia-tile, provider resolver, cache, acquisition and delivery. Both HTTP parts are required, finite, independently bounded, and checked against the epoch bounds using the precise representation. All scalar aliases are rejected alongside the pair.

original defects closed.defect: Python datetime cannot represent UTC leap seconds; the final fraction of a leap can silently round to normal midnight even with Astropy strict conversion.
original defects closed.closure: Check native two-part UTC leap intervals before datetime conversion. Return UnsupportedUTCInstant/code unsupported_utc_instant and HTTP 422/retryable=false. Scalar ambiguity returns HTTP 400/retryable=false. OpenAPI documents both and gives the Astropy component input path.

original defects closed.defect: Existing tests only demonstrated discarded identity and bypassed leap-midnight acquisition.
original defects closed.closure: Independent literal UTC/TAI offsets at 1990, 2012, 2015 and 2017 boundaries test both boundaries, actual normal midnights, independently TAI-origin midnights, preceding ordinary instants, genuine leap interiors and a final 0.1 us leap fraction. Live ASGI tests run real provider/cache code with deterministic upstream fixtures; ordinary and leap instants sharing one scalar cannot reuse each other, and two ordinary precise instants sharing a scalar keep separate cache keys. Ordinary scalar conversion retains its existing half-ULP plus datetime quantization bounds.

exact remaining boundaries: This closes the assigned time-policy/precision child, not all of SCN-048. No production TLS transport, deployed proxy/authentication/gateway operation or owner URL evidence was supplied by this task.
Provider/frame/spatial calibration and continuous archive availability remain separate solar acceptance work. Deterministic upstream ASGI fixtures do not certify those properties.
Genuine UTC leap instants are intentionally unsupported at the Python datetime/AIA provider boundary and are explicitly rejected; no full leap-second provider support is claimed.

Precise HTTP input is supported at /solar/realtime/aia-tile. Synthetic solar physics/engine APIs retain their existing labelled scalar-TDB contract; they are not passed through the UTC provider adapter.

The concurrently updated GONG acquire path remains a scalar-only API. Its ordinary requests pass regressions and its leap-boundary/interior calls now receive the same typed time errors. No precise GONG provenance/API support is claimed; see solar-handoff.json if that capability is later required.

Classification uses the active ERFA positive-leap schedule and Astropy two-part precision. No hypothetical future leap schedule or new negative-leap certification is claimed. Ordinary datetime output remains limited to its documented one-microsecond resolution.
